environment.description: Same Kubernetes pod running OpenJDK 17 on Ubuntu 22.04 with runc. Container uses a custom OCI runtime seccomp profile loaded via annotation 'container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/imageservice: runtime/default' and a seccomp profile specified at pod level via 'securityContext.seccompProfile.type: Localhost' pointing to '/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/imageservice-hardened.json'. The profile is a SCMP_ACT_ERRNO default-deny with explicit SCMP_ACT_ALLOW for a curated syscall allowlist. Notably, the allowlist permits read, write, mmap, mprotect, brk, futex, close, fstat, openat, lseek, getpid, clock_gettime, epoll_ctl, epoll_wait, accept4 (for Tomcat), and ~40 other operational syscalls. The profile uses SCMP_ACT_ERRNO (returning EPERM) for execve, execveat, ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, socket (AF_INET with SOCK_STREAM only allowed via conditional on accept4 already-open FDs), connect, bind, and sendmsg/recvmsg with SCM_RIGHTS. The native .so is compiled with -fno-stack-protector and ASLR remains disabled, so the overflow and ROP chain construction remain viable, but any payload attempting code execution or reverse shell establishment is blocked at the kernel level.

config.socket_restriction: only accept4 on pre-bound server FDs, no new socket() calls
config.note: overflow still achievable but post-exploitation syscalls blocked
